title: Critical Skills Employment Permit for Ireland: a 2-year job offer in a critical skills occupation paying at least €40,904 a year, or any eligible job paying €68,911

sources.title: Employment Permits Act 2024, s. 7(1): a foreign national shall not be in employment in the State except in accordance with an employment permit
Employment Permits Act 2024, s. 8(1)(e): section 7 does not apply to a foreign national entitled to enter and work in the State under the treaties governing the European Union
Immigration Act 1999, s. 1(1): a non-national is an alien under the Aliens Act 1935, other than an alien whom an order under s. 10 of that Act exempts from all of it
Aliens (Exemption) Order 1999 (S.I. No. 97 of 1999), art. 3: every citizen of the United Kingdom is exempted from all the provisions of the Aliens Act 1935
Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment: non-EEA nationals need an employment permit; Swiss nationals work in Ireland without one under the 2001 Act on free movement with Switzerland
Employment Permits Act 2024, s. 22(1): no permit unless 50 per cent or more of the employees are nationals of the EEA, Switzerland or the United Kingdom, with exceptions
Employment Permits Regulations 2024 (S.I. No. 444 of 2024), regs. 28 and 29: a minimum period of employment of 2 years and a minimum of 20 hours of work each week
Employment Permits Regulations 2024 (S.I. No. 444 of 2024), reg. 27: a relevant third level degree; for a nurse, midwife or radiographer, one their registration board accepts
S.I. No. 643 of 2025, regs. 2, 4 to 7 and 21 (Schedule 8, Part 1), from 1 March 2026: €40,904, €36,848 with a level 8 degree of the last 12 months, €68,911, hourly rates, public sector pay agreements
S.I. No. 213 of 2026, reg. 4, made 13 May 2026: a new Schedule 3, the critical skills occupations, including ICT professionals in SOC 2133 to 2139 such as software developers
S.I. No. 558 of 2026, regs. 6 and 7, made 28 October 2026: Schedule 3 and the ineligible list in Schedule 4 replaced again; ICT professionals in SOC 2133 to 2139 stay on Schedule 3

Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Critical Skills Employment Permit: €40,904, €36,848, €68,911, public sector pay agreements, 2-year job offer, 50% rule, immediate family reunification
Policy Document on Non-EEA Family Reunification (12 June 2026), paras. 1.5.1, 6.3 and 10.8: a Critical Skills Employment Permit holder's spouse, partner and minor children may come on arrival
Family Reunification Policy, paras. 7.5 and 7.10: a spouse or civil partner must be 18 or over at application; a recognised civil partnership counts as marriage
Family Reunification Policy, glossary and paras. 7.12 to 7.13: a de facto partner 18 or over, in a relationship akin to marriage with at least 2 years of cohabitation before applying
Family Reunification Policy, paras. 7.21, 7.22, 7.24, 7.26 and 8.2: biological, adopted or step-children, unmarried and under 18; stepchildren must be full-time members of the household
Immigration Service Delivery: amendments to the non-EEA Family Reunification Policy take effect from 12 June 2026
Immigration Service Delivery, Join non EEA family member: a Category B sponsor, such as a Critical Skills Employment Permit holder, may be joined by a spouse, civil or de facto partner or minor child

S.I. No. 444 of 2024, reg. 7, Schedule 1: €1,000 for a critical skills employment permit; no fee for a registered charity or an EEA, Swiss or UK national's spouse or civil partner; 90% back on refusal
Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Fees for Employment Permits: €1,000 for a Critical Skills Employment Permit of up to 24 months
Immigration Act 2004 (Registration Certificate Fee) Regulations 2025 (S.I. No. 421 of 2025), regs. 3 and 4: €300 for a registration certificate, waived for a person under the age of 18 years
Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Critical Skills Employment Permit, renewals: a holder can apply for a Stamp 4 permission, granted for 2 years, then renewable

requirements.title: Not a citizen of Ireland, another EU or EEA state, Switzerland or the United Kingdom: they work in Ireland without an employment permit

assessments.title: A job offer of at least 2 years and at least 20 hours of work each week
An employer at least half of whose employees are EEA, Swiss or UK nationals, save the exceptions of the act
Pay of at least €40,904 a year and €20.17 an hour in a critical skills occupation, or at least €68,911 a year and €33.98 an hour in any other eligible job
Critical skills occupation, not a nurse, midwife or radiographer: €36,848 a year and €18.17 an hour are enough with a degree at level 8 or higher, or equivalent, from the 12 months before applying
A critical skills job bound by a public sector pay agreement, or by a Workplace Relations Commission agreement linked to one, needs that agreement's pay instead of the €40,904 or €36,848 threshold
A relevant third level degree (a nurse, midwife or radiographer: a degree or diploma their registration board accepts); for a job paying €68,911 or more, a relevant degree or the experience

dependents.title: Spouse or civil partner aged 18 or over
De facto partner aged 18 or over, after 2 years together; a shorter relationship, which may be a civil partnership: possible
Children under 18 and unmarried, biological or adopted; that Irish law recognises an adoption is not checked
The spouse or civil partner's children under 18 and unmarried, as stepchildren; living full time in the household is not checked

costs.title: Permit application fee, paid by the applicant, 90% returned on refusal or withdrawal; not checked: no fee for a registered charity or for the spouse or civil partner of an EEA, Swiss or UK national
Fee for the registration certificate (IRP card) on registering the immigration permission, €300; the waivers in reg. 4 are not checked
Fee for the registration certificate of each family member aged 18 or over, €300; waived for a person under the age of 18 years

durations.title: Critical Skills Employment Permit of up to 24 months, for which the €1,000 fee is paid
Stamp 4 permission after the permit, to live and work without an employment permit: 2 years, then renewable
